title: Sectionwise short exactness implies short exactness of internal sheaf modules
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a site whose underlying category is essentially small relative to the universe of the abelian groups used as coefficients. Give $\mathcal B=\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C,\mathrm{Ab})$ the sheafified objectwise tensor over $\mathbf Z$ of [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor]. Let $\mathcal R$ be a ring object of $\mathcal B$ [sk-def-sfb-ring-object], and use internal left module objects and their forgetful functor $U:\operatorname{Mod}_{\mathcal R}(\mathcal B)\to\mathcal B$ as in [sk-def-sfb-module-objects]. Let $M_0,M_1,M_2$ be such internal modules and let $F:M_0\to M_1$ and $G:M_1\to M_2$ be internal module morphisms with $G\circ F=0$. Suppose that for every object $V$ of $\mathcal C$ the sequence of abelian groups
$$0\longrightarrow U(M_0)(V)\xrightarrow{U(F)_V}U(M_1)(V)\xrightarrow{U(G)_V}U(M_2)(V)\longrightarrow0$$
is short exact. Then the sequence of underlying abelian presheaves is short exact, the sequence of underlying abelian sheaves is short exact, and
$$0\longrightarrow M_0\xrightarrow{F}M_1\xrightarrow{G}M_2\longrightarrow0$$
is short exact in the abelian category $\operatorname{Mod}_{\mathcal R}(\mathcal B)$ of [lem-sfb-modobj-abelian] (its hypotheses hold by the closedness in [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor]), with these prescribed arrows. Here short exactness is as in [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence].

source.place: On the point: "So the sequence of condensed ... modules is exact"; the passage from sectionwise short exactness to internal-module short exactness, using the forgetful functor and exact abelian sheafification as in the landed proof, not the internal/sectionwise equivalence.

proof.text: Write $P_i=\iota U(M_i)$, $f=\iota U(F)$ and $g=\iota U(G)$, where $\iota$ is the sheaf inclusion. By [lem-weil-pbc-abelian-presheaves-evaluation-exact], abelian presheaves form an abelian category, and their kernels and cokernels are computed sectionwise. Thus $\ker f(V)=0$ and $\operatorname{coker}g(V)=0$ by the hypothesis. Moreover the image presheaf of $f$, computed as the kernel of its sectionwise cokernel, has value $\operatorname{im}f_V=\ker g_V$. These are equal subpresheaves, since both carry the restrictions inherited from $P_1$. Consequently $0\to P_0\xrightarrow fP_1\xrightarrow gP_2\to0$ is short exact by [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence].

By [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-exact], abelian sheafification $a$ preserves finite limits and colimits. Hence it preserves kernels and cokernels, and images expressed as kernels of cokernels; applying it to step 1 gives a short exact sequence with arrows $a(f),a(g)$. The sheaf category is abelian by [lem-sfb-abelian-sheaves-left-exact-reflector], applied with coefficient category $\mathrm{Ab}$ and this left exact reflector. The essentially small site is replaced, if needed, by its small model in the coefficient universe, with the transported topology; restriction along the equivalence bijects matching families and preserves all the stated diagrams. By [lem-weil-pbc-presheaf-finite-limits-objectwise], the counits $\epsilon_i:a\iota U(M_i)\xrightarrow{\sim}U(M_i)$ are isomorphisms. Their naturality says $\epsilon_1a(f)=U(F)\epsilon_0$ and $\epsilon_2a(g)=U(G)\epsilon_1$. These identify the sheafified sequence with the sequence of underlying sheaves with precisely the prescribed arrows, proving the second conclusion.

The tensor functors in $\mathcal B$ preserve colimits by closedness in [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor]. They are additive by [lem-sfb-preserving-colimits-additive], since $\mathcal B$ is abelian by step 2. In particular $\mathcal R\otimes-$ preserves finite colimits. Thus all hypotheses of [lem-sfb-modobj-abelian] hold and $\operatorname{Mod}_{\mathcal R}(\mathcal B)$ is abelian. Under exactly these hypotheses [lem-sfb-modobj-forget-left-exact] and [lem-sfb-modobj-forget-right-exact] say that $U$ preserves finite limits and finite colimits.

proof.text: The functor $U$ preserves zero morphisms: it preserves the terminal object by step 3, and a terminal object in either abelian category is a zero object; a zero morphism factors through that object. It is faithful by [lem-sfb-modobj-forget-faithful]. It also reflects isomorphisms directly from [sk-def-sfb-module-objects]: if a module map $h:M\to N$ has underlying inverse $k$, its action equation is $h\gamma_M=\gamma_N(\mathcal R\otimes h)$. Composing on the left with $k$ and on the right with $\mathcal R\otimes k$ gives $\gamma_M(\mathcal R\otimes k)=k\gamma_N$. Thus $k$ is a module map and its two inverse equations are those of the underlying maps. This proves reflection without any identification with sectionwise ring-module sheaves.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-jointly-reflect-short-exact] to the one-element family consisting of $U$. Both categories are abelian by steps 2--3; $U$ preserves finite limits and finite colimits by step 3 and zero morphisms by step 4; and this singleton family reflects isomorphisms by step 4. The short complex is $(M_0\xrightarrow F M_1\xrightarrow G M_2)$ with the given zero composite. Step 2 supplies short exactness of its image under $U$. The reverse implication of the cited node therefore proves short exactness of this very internal-module sequence. Together with steps 1 and 2 this proves every clause.
